_note: arm 5 (fields-at-creation). (i) OUTAGE-IMMUNITY PREMISE: a create carrying an inline `fields` array was sent while the /fields WRITE family was probed in the same seconds on the same table path. The kitted create reported `applied` — verified by the created table's own field list, never by code:0 — and the same-window POST .../fields control answered `9499` ('Invalid parameter type in param: TableId. Invalid parameter value: "tblnHfrepWfI8RfD". Please check and modify accordingly.'). Read the two together: a kitted create that applied beside a 9499 control is the premise HOLDING; a kitted create that dropped or failed beside a code:0 control refutes it, and the capability still ships either way because it is the right shape for the surface independent of any outage. (ii) PRIMARY COLUMN: after the kitted create the columns flagged is_primary were ['ld336-title']; the kit's first entry BECAME the primary: True. True is what probe ld336-02 measured across nine cases — a kitted create does NOT also get the locale-named default column, so entry 0 of the array is the column the rows are keyed by and the array's ORDER is a decision.

response.shipped_batch_verb_refuses_a_kit: `batch_create_tables` does not author columns. Lark's batch route ACCEPTS a per-table `fields` array, answers code:0, and creates every table WITHOUT it — each one arrives with the locale-named default primary column and none of the kit. That was measured on the shipped path and again on a hand-written body through the raw HTTP core, so it is the server's behaviour and not something this library can send its way around; forwarding the array anyway would be shipping a silent no-op, which is exactly what R12 forbids. Use one `create_table(app_token, name, fields=[...])` per table — that route DOES author the kit, and each is still a single call. Nothing was sent.
